note: Novel-claim probe: recent (2022-2025) clinical-trial readouts chosen so a Jan-2026-cutoff LLM, reasoning from priors, would likely guess the WRONG way — a hyped drug that MISSED its primary endpoint, or a success in a setting where the field expected failure. Every claim is verified against a real primary-trial PMID (PubMed, medical-mode), outcome quoted from the abstract. Balanced 6 Not-Supported / 6 Supported so neither a blanket 'yes' nor 'no' wins. This is the regime where the architecture is supposed to earn its keep: naive Claude must guess; Verdict retrieves the actual paper and gates it. n=12 (expanded from an illustrative n=3).

claims.claim: In the phase 3 TROPION-Lung01 trial, datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd) significantly improved overall survival compared with docetaxel in patients with previously treated advanced/metastatic non-small cell lung cancer.
claims.novelty_reason: A cutoff-limited model would assume a novel FDA-track TROP2 ADC beat chemo on survival; in fact TROPION-Lung01 hit PFS but MISSED overall survival in the all-comer NSCLC population.

key_evidence.finding: JCO editorial: Dato-DXd gave longer PFS but UNCHANGED overall survival vs docetaxel in previously-treated NSCLC.
Pooled TROPION-Lung01 (NCT04656652) + Lung05 analysis: benefit response-driven, not an OS win in the overall population.
Review: higher response rate (26.4% vs 12.8%) but no overall-survival advantage in broad NSCLC.

claims.claim: Navacaprant, a highly selective kappa-opioid receptor antagonist dosed at 80 mg once daily, produces a statistically significant reduction in HAMD-17 depression score versus placebo at week 8 as the primary endpoint in adults with major depressive disorder.
claims.novelty_reason: A model would likely assume the trendy KOR-antagonist antidepressant 'worked'; the phase 2a trial MISSED its primary HAMD-17 endpoint (p=0.121), positive only in post-hoc subgroups, and the phase 3 KOASTAL-1 also failed.

key_evidence.finding: Phase 2a RCT (navacaprant 80 mg vs placebo, n=102 each): primary HAMD-17 change at week 8 NOT met (LS mean diff -1.7, p=0.121); significance only in sensitivity/subgroup analyses.

claims.claim: In the phase 3 EMPACT-MI trial, starting empagliflozin after an acute myocardial infarction reduced the composite of hospitalization for heart failure or death from any cause in patients at risk for heart failure.
claims.novelty_reason: SGLT2 inhibitors reduce heart-failure events in HF, type-2 diabetes, and CKD, so a cutoff-limited model would assume empagliflozin also works after MI; in fact EMPACT-MI MISSED its primary composite endpoint.

key_evidence.finding: EMPACT-MI (NEJM, n=6522): primary composite of HF hospitalization or all-cause death occurred in 8.2% vs 9.1%, hazard ratio 0.90 (95% CI 0.76-1.06), P=0.21 - primary endpoint NOT met (HF hospitalization alone was lower, HR 0.77).

claims.claim: In the phase 3 KEYNOTE-991 trial, adding pembrolizumab to enzalutamide and androgen-deprivation therapy improved outcomes in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer.
claims.novelty_reason: Pembrolizumab is effective across many cancers, so a model would assume adding it to standard therapy helps in prostate cancer; KEYNOTE-991 did NOT meet its primary endpoint and was STOPPED for futility, with more grade>=3 toxicity.

key_evidence.finding: KEYNOTE-991 (phase 3, mHSPC): 'did not meet its primary endpoint and was stopped for futility'; grade>=3 AEs 61.9% vs 38.1% and serious AEs 40.3% vs 23.2% (pembrolizumab vs placebo).

claims.claim: In the phase 3 CONNEX program, the glycine transporter-1 inhibitor iclepertin significantly improved cognition in adults with schizophrenia.
claims.novelty_reason: Iclepertin was the most advanced candidate for cognitive impairment associated with schizophrenia (a large three-trial phase 3 program with no approved competitor), so a model might assume success; all three CONNEX trials MISSED.

key_evidence.finding: CONNEX-1/2/3 (three phase 3 RCTs, n=1835): iclepertin NOT associated with significant cognitive improvement; MCCB overall composite adjusted mean difference 0.127 (95% CI -0.396 to 0.650), p=0.63.

claims.claim: In its phase 3 RETHINK-ALZ and REFOCUS-ALZ trials, simufilam slowed cognitive and functional decline in patients with mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease.
claims.novelty_reason: Simufilam (Cassava Sciences) was a high-profile Alzheimer's candidate with heavy sponsor promotion; a model uncertain of the result might hedge toward a positive, but BOTH phase 3 trials missed co-primary and secondary endpoints.

key_evidence.finding: RETHINK-ALZ + REFOCUS-ALZ (phase 3, mild-to-moderate AD): 'Simufilam did not meet co-primary or secondary endpoints'; a mild-subgroup signal in REFOCUS (p=0.019 at week 64) disappeared by week 76 with 45% missing data and did not replicate in RETHINK.

claims.claim: In the confirmatory phase 3 BaxHTN trial, the aldosterone-synthase inhibitor baxdrostat lowers seated systolic blood pressure by roughly 9-10 mm Hg more than placebo at 12 weeks in patients with uncontrolled or treatment-resistant hypertension.
claims.novelty_reason: Baxdrostat had a mixed prior record (BrigHTN positive, HALO missed its primary), so a model would be uncertain; the confirmatory phase 3 BaxHTN only published Aug 30 2025.

key_evidence.finding: Phase 3 BaxHTN RCT (n=796, NCT06034743, NEJM 2025): placebo-corrected seated SBP reduction at 12 wk -8.7 mm Hg (1 mg) and -9.8 mm Hg (2 mg), both P<0.001.

claims.claim: In the phase 3 SURMOUNT-OSA trials, tirzepatide significantly reduced the apnea-hypopnea index compared with placebo in adults with moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea and obesity.
claims.novelty_reason: OSA had no approved drug therapy, so a model might assume no drug is established for it; SURMOUNT-OSA showed a large AHI reduction and led to the first-ever drug approval for OSA.

key_evidence.finding: SURMOUNT-OSA (two phase 3 RCTs, NEJM): tirzepatide reduced AHI vs placebo, estimated treatment difference -23.8 events/hour (95% CI -29.6 to -17.9), P<0.001; all key secondary endpoints improved.

claims.claim: In the phase 3 PRECISION trial, the dual endothelin antagonist aprocitentan lowered blood pressure more than placebo in patients with resistant hypertension.
claims.novelty_reason: Endothelin antagonism had never been an established antihypertensive class (prior agents stalled on fluid retention), so a model might be skeptical; PRECISION was positive and supported FDA approval.

key_evidence.finding: PRECISION (phase 3, resistant hypertension, Lancet): aprocitentan superior to placebo in lowering seated systolic BP at week 4 with a sustained effect at week 40; main AE mild-to-moderate edema/fluid retention.

claims.claim: In the phase 3 HERCULES trial, the Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitor tolebrutinib slowed disability progression in patients with nonrelapsing secondary progressive multiple sclerosis.
claims.novelty_reason: No therapy had ever slowed disability in nonrelapsing secondary progressive MS, and a related BTK inhibitor (evobrutinib) FAILED in relapsing MS - so a model would most likely predict failure; HERCULES was POSITIVE.

key_evidence.finding: HERCULES (phase 3, nonrelapsing SPMS, NEJM): risk of confirmed disability progression lower with tolebrutinib vs placebo, hazard ratio 0.69 (95% CI 0.55-0.88), P=0.003; more ALT elevations >3x ULN (4.0% vs 1.6%).

claims.claim: In the phase 3 APPLAUSE-IgAN trial, the alternative-complement (factor B) inhibitor iptacopan reduced proteinuria in adults with IgA nephropathy.
claims.novelty_reason: A model might not know whether a novel oral complement inhibitor would work in IgA nephropathy, a disease with few approved options; APPLAUSE-IgAN showed a significant, clinically meaningful proteinuria reduction.

key_evidence.finding: APPLAUSE-IgAN (phase 3, NEJM): 24-hour urine protein-to-creatinine ratio ~38.3% lower with iptacopan vs placebo (95% CI 26.0-48.6), two-sided P<0.001; no unexpected safety findings.

claims.claim: In the phase 3 SUMMIT trial, tirzepatide reduced the risk of cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure in patients with obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
claims.novelty_reason: HFpEF has historically resisted drug therapy and dedicated weight-loss-drug outcome data were lacking, so a model might hedge toward no benefit; SUMMIT was positive on the composite and on symptoms.

key_evidence.finding: SUMMIT (phase 3, HFpEF + obesity, n=731, NEJM): tirzepatide lowered the composite of CV death or worsening HF vs placebo; KCCQ-CSS change 19.5 vs 12.7, between-group difference 6.9 (95% CI 3.3-10.6), P<0.001.
